title: The small trend line uses days, weeks or months by range length
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide at 100% zoom (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  • {Location-A} has invoices spread over the last twelve months, so the Revenue tile shows an amount above $0.00 on Last 12 Months.
  • This month, at least two days at {Location-A} have clocked time on invoiced work, with a day between them that has no clocked time at all, {Day-A} (for example a Sunday).
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 31 days", and click Apply.
  3. Count the points (corners) on the Revenue trend line.
  4. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 32 days", and click Apply. Count the points.
  5. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 182 days", and click Apply. Count the points.
  6. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 183 days", and click Apply. Count the points.
  7. Set the Revenue pill to Last 12 Months and click View details on Revenue.
  8. Compare the Revenue trend line's shape with the monthly bars in the Revenue chart.
  9. Set the Billing Efficiency pill to This Month and look at its trend line at {Day-A}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: 31 days draws exactly 31 points, one for every day, including days with no sales: on Revenue a day with no sales is a point at $0, not a gap.
  • Step 4: 32 days draws one point per week (about 5 points).
  • Step 5: 182 days still draws one point per week (about 26 points).
  • Step 6: 183 days draws one point per month (about 7 points).
  • Steps 7 and 8: On Last 12 Months the trend line has 12 points, and they rise and fall exactly like the 12 monthly bars in the expanded Revenue chart. No point disagrees with the bar for the same month.
  • Step 9: At {Day-A} the Billing Efficiency line has a gap: it breaks and resumes. It is not drawn down to zero and the days either side are not joined across the gap.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles), with SV-9579 (Story 7), SV-9578 (Story 6) and SV-9581 (Story 9); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S4-R10 and S4-R11 (unchanged since version 42), S4-R11a (added in version 43 on 9 Oct 2026), S7-R2a, S6-R3a and S9-R9 (added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 (15:06 UTC) by Chris Ward; the spec's change log (version 46) lists it under 2026-10-14); read 14 Oct 2026. The 731-day and 732-day ranges were removed because a tile's calendar now allows at most 366 days (S7-R2a, Chris Ward's answer 3 of 14 Oct 2026), so the switch to one point per quarter cannot be reached from a tile. Design canvas board 03_Range_After for the date pill, calendar and "Range: N days" readout. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R10: “The sparkline shows the tile's measure trending over the selected range.”
  • S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).”
  • S4-R11a: “On Revenue and the count tiles, a bucket with no sales is a point at 0. Only a ratio tile's "-" (S3-E3) contributes no point.”
  • S7-R2a: “The control is the same date picker the reports use. Besides the nine presets it offers a calendar for choosing a custom range of up to 366 days, the same limit the reports apply, and a Today button inside the calendar. Today is part of the calendar, not a tenth preset. A custom range is not remembered between visits (S7-R8), and the report opened from the tile shows it as "Custom" (S10-E1).”
  • S6-R3a: “The expanded Revenue chart covers the tile's own date range (S7-R5), with one bar per day, week, month or quarter chosen from the length of the range by the same rule as the sparkline (S4-R11). Last 12 Months shows twelve monthly bars; This Month shows daily bars.”
  • S9-R9: “In an expanded chart, a month with no value is drawn as a dashed line joining the points on either side of it. This is how these charts already draw in production. A gap in the line applies only to the sparkline on a tile (S4-R11).”
